annotations.description: Siege Striker as a 1/1 double strike with no other creatures to tap applies only 2 damage per attack, compared to Makeshift Battalion's 3 damage as a 3/2. With an empty board, Battalion provides significantly more immediate pressure and is a better body against potential blockers.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Siege Striker (1/1 double strike) as first creature with no other creatures to support its tap ability
annotations.betterLine: Cast Makeshift Battalion (3/2) for better immediate board presence and pressure, especially against a land-light opponent where aggression is key

annotations.description: GLM47 declined to attack with Siege Striker when the opponent had no untapped creatures (Merrow Reejerey is sick) and no untapped lands to cast tricks. Siege Striker could attack, tap Makeshift Battalion (sick but still tappable) to become 2/2 with double strike, dealing 4 unblockable damage for free.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not declare any attackers, passing the combat phase entirely.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Siege Striker, tap Makeshift Battalion to its trigger, making it a 2/2 double striker dealing 4 free damage to the opponent who has no blocks and no mana for tricks.

annotations.description: Gem3F declined to attack with Merrow Reejerey (3/3) when the opponent had all lands tapped and only a 1/1 Siege Striker as a potential blocker. There was zero risk of combat tricks and the attack would deal 3 free damage (opponent won't profitably block with a 1/1 into a 3/3).
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Merrow Reejerey for 3 damage. The opponent either takes 3 or chump blocks with Siege Striker, both favorable outcomes with no mana open for tricks.

annotations.description: Opponent has all lands tapped and only one non-summoning-sick blocker. Not attacking misses an opportunity to deal free damage or force an unfavorable block. With two attackers and only one blocker, at least 2-3 damage gets through guaranteed.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures despite opponent being tapped out.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Makeshift Battalion and Siege Striker. Opponent can only block one - guaranteeing at least 2 damage (Siege Striker double strike) or 3 damage (Battalion) gets through, while opponent's lands are tapped preventing any tricks.

annotations.description: GLM47 declined to block either Merrow Reejerey with Makeshift Battalion. Both Reejereys are 3/3 (lord buffs). Blocking one would trade the 3/2 Battalion for a Reejerey (both die to 3 damage), and the surviving Reejerey would have already dealt its 3 combat damage. By not blocking, GLM47 takes 6 damage instead of 3, and leaves both Merfolk lords on the battlefield. Killing a Reejerey is especially valuable because it removes a lord effect, weakening all other Merfolk the opponent plays, and the opponent has 6 cards in hand likely containing more Merfolk.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to block, taking 6 damage from two 3/3 Merrow Reejereys.
annotations.betterLine: Block one Merrow Reejerey with Makeshift Battalion to trade and take only 3 damage. This removes a dangerous lord creature and weakens the opponent's future Merfolk plays.

annotations.description: With Cathars' Crusade in play, sequencing matters significantly. Playing the cheaper Siege Striker (3 mana) this turn and Bulwark Giant next turn would yield two separate Cathars' Crusade triggers across two turns, putting more total +1/+1 counters on the team. Siege Striker with double strike becomes an enormous threat with even one counter. Playing Bulwark Giant first means next turn Siege Striker enters and only gets one round of counters on fewer future creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Bulwark Giant for 6 mana, getting one Cathars' Crusade trigger and 5 life.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Siege Striker for 3 mana this turn (one Crusade trigger, making it a 2/2 double striker and Battalion a 4/3), then cast Bulwark Giant next turn for a second Crusade trigger, maximizing counter distribution and presenting a lethal double-strike threat sooner.

annotations.description: Tapped the opponent's Bulwark Giant with Merrow Reejerey's trigger, but the Giant is sick (summoning sickness) and can't attack or use tap abilities anyway, so tapping it accomplishes nothing. They should have untapped one of their own tapped lands to gain access to more mana. With two Reejerey triggers (from two Reejereys), they could untap two lands and potentially hold up Lookout's Dispersal (3 mana counterspell) or have mana for other responses.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Bulwark Giant (sick creature) to tap it with Reejerey trigger
annotations.betterLine: Untap one of their own tapped Islands or Thriving Isle to have mana available for interaction, particularly working toward having 3 mana for Lookout's Dispersal with the second Reejerey trigger

annotations.description: Declined to tap the opponent's 4/7 Bulwark Giant with Merrow Reejerey's trigger before combat. Tapping it would remove a massive blocker, allowing Merfolk to connect for combat damage and trigger Seafloor Oracle's card draw. There is zero downside to tapping an opponent's creature here.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to tap Bulwark Giant (chose False)
annotations.betterLine: Tap the opponent's Bulwark Giant with the Reejerey trigger to remove it as a blocker, enabling more combat damage and Seafloor Oracle card draws.

annotations.description: The Merrow Reejerey trigger from casting Seafloor Oracle lets the player tap or untap any permanent. Choosing to untap a Merrow Reejerey (which doesn't produce mana) instead of untapping an Island wastes the opportunity to chain Merfolk spells. Untapping an Island would provide mana to cast Triton Shorestalker ({U}), which would trigger the other Reejerey to untap another land, enabling further plays.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to untap Merrow Reejerey, which doesn't produce mana or enable further plays.
annotations.betterLine: Untap an Island to get {U}, enabling casting Triton Shorestalker, which chains more Reejerey triggers to untap more lands and potentially cast additional spells like Heirloom Blade or set up for future turns.

annotations.description: Untapping Merrow Reejerey instead of an Island. The Reejerey will untap naturally during the next untap step, so untapping it now provides minimal value (just an extra blocker this turn cycle). Untapping an Island instead would provide mana to hold up interaction like Lookout's Dispersal (3 mana without Pirate discount) or other responses during the opponent's turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to untap Merrow Reejerey with the first Reejerey trigger
annotations.betterLine: Untap an Island to have mana available for interaction. With the second Reejerey trigger, untap another Island to maximize available mana for holding up countermagic or instant-speed plays.

annotations.description: Gem3F Tinker passed on countering Heirloom Blade with Lookout's Dispersal while the opponent had only 1 untapped land (can't pay {4}). Heirloom Blade equipped to Patron of the Valiant (flying) makes it 8/6 flying - a serious threat that Gem3F has limited ways to block. The death trigger also chains into another creature with Cathars' Crusade out, making the opponent's board increasingly dangerous.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, allowing Heirloom Blade to resolve
annotations.betterLine: Cast Lookout's Dispersal to counter Heirloom Blade. The opponent has only 1 untapped land and cannot pay {4}, making it a hard counter. This prevents a massive flying threat and denies the valuable death trigger.
